_provenance: Plain-language glossary for daily public users. Definitions derived from IUDP v3 Ch1-2 and MSIP format usage. English only for release 1; Nepali arrives with the full translation release. Missing or wrong? Edit data/glossary.json — js/glossary.js picks it up on reload.

terms.en: Integrated Urban Development Plan — the municipality's statutory 15-year plan (2026–2041). It decides where the town grows, what gets built, in which phase, and who pays.
Municipal Sector Investment Plan — the standard federal format that turns sector plans into a costed, phased, fundable project list. The NPR 1,040 crore envelope is the MSIP working figure.
Logical Framework Approach — a planning table that states a project's goal, purpose, outputs, how each will be measured (OVI), and what must stay true for it to work (assumptions).
Department of Urban Development and Building Construction — the federal body whose service standards (Annex A norms) are used here to measure the gap between what Baglung has and what it should have.
Right-of-way — the legal width of land reserved for a road. Baglung's core bazaar roads are 5–8 m wide against the national standard of 10–30 m, which is why drains and footpaths don't fit.
Detailed Project Report — the engineering document (drawings, measurements, cost estimate) prepared before a project can actually be tendered and built.
Bill of Quantities — the item-by-item cost list of everything a construction project needs. The physical sector's NPR 551.3 cr figure is a sector-internal BOQ estimate.
Public-Private Partnership — a project delivered jointly by the municipality and private investors, so public money buys less and private capital carries more of the cost and risk.
Geographic Information System — software that layers map data (population, flood risk, roads, land use) so planning decisions are made on evidence about specific places, not averages.
National Population and Housing Census — Nepal's official every-10-years count (latest: 2021). All ward population and household figures in this plan trace to it or to municipal records.
Internal Rate of Return — an investor's yardstick: the yearly return a project is expected to earn. The bungy flagship's IRR of 32% means it should pay back well above borrowing cost.
Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, Threats — the standard four-box analysis of a place or sector used before choosing a strategy.
Ward — the smallest administrative unit of the municipality. Baglung has 14 wards; each has a ward office and an elected representative.
Palika — Nepali for local government body. Baglung Nagarpalika means Baglung Municipality, the urban palika governing all 14 wards.
Tole — a neighbourhood or cluster of households within a ward, usually with its own name, committee and shared concerns.
Provenance — where a number comes from and who has authority over it. Every figure in this plan carries its source; conflicts between documents are logged, never silently resolved.
Tukra — small fragmented ward-level works funded by tiny individual allocations. Pooling tukra budgets into trunk corridors is a core strategy of this plan.
MLD — million litres per day (water supply volume). lpcd — litres per capita per day (the personal usage standard, set at 120 in the demand model).
Cold chain — refrigerated storage and transport that keeps farm produce fresh from field to market, letting hill farmers sell beyond the same-day bazaar.
Concession — the municipality licenses a private operator to run a public asset (like the rafting corridor) for a fixed term, in exchange for fees, service standards and shared revenue.
Own source revenue — money the municipality raises itself (property tax, service fees, rents) rather than receiving as federal or provincial grants. Growing it is the financial plan's core goal.
